text:
walking part 2 / boosting FY miles guidance

it turns out that walking 4-5 miles is good, 6-7 miles is better, 8-9 is better, and 10 is even better

this is proof that God exists and loves us

more miles = you sleep better, you think clearer, you lose weight, you get sun, you get fresh air

so, the new miles guidance is 10 miles a day

it's a lot, but its doable, its worth it, and u break it down something like:

-early AM: try to knock out 5. wake up earlier if u have to

-9-10 AM: I always do the shittiest/most painful work first thing in the AM, so by 9-10 my head hurts and I need a walk. you can knock out 2-3 here...move at a brisk pace and do whatever 30 mins gets u

-12 PM: I try and jam every single possible phone call for noon, and then take it while walking outside...knock out 2-3 more.

-2-3 PM: any in-person meeting, I try and jam it into this slot, and the "meeting" consists of walking around.

That's how you get to somewhere close to 10 miles on a daily basis

With health, the body and mind feel like they hit peak performance once u string together 1-2 weeks of doing everything right

I played too much Halo 2 so I view everything as sprees

If you can get pretty good sleep for 1-2 weeks straight, that's a Sleeping Spree and u feel like a God

gym isn't a spree, u gotta be in there 24/7/365...no days off. same for diet, u just eat the same thing every day.

but walking 10 miles, u can definitely qualify that for Killing Spree, Splatter Spree, Kilimanjaro, maybe Killtacular...whatever the highest level was in Halo

the only other one which is real, is Ocean Spree

find a half hour during the day, at any point, and make it happen

if you swim in the ocean every single day for 1-2 weeks, and get decent sleep, and walk 10 miles, ur mind and ur emotions are almost in a blissful Zen-like state

bad news hits u and it just bounces off, u don't feel stress

never underestimate the impact of your habits and lifestyle, on your mental and your emotional state

most of what feels like anxiety/depression, is caused by bad fucking habits

you can test this by how you feel when you only get 1-2 hours of sleep

you are anxious and irritable and grumpy all day, your diet is fucked up, your impulse control is fucked up...like, everything is just a mess, you really can't trust yourself on days like those

you find yourself getting anxious over issues that are already resolved, anxiety to me = "new worries over old issues," but it's like a fake, fugazi-ass worry

once u get ur habits right, all that shit disappears, its bad-habit driven anxiety and not "actual life problem" anxiety

but if u can fit in 10 miles, all the other shit is gonna fall into place

you will sleep better, you will eat less, you'll lose weight, everything else falls into place if you are constantly in motion...God just seems to have designed us that way

The Eminent Dead figured this out ages ago, I think Rousseau walked 8 miles a day, John Adams was good for 5-10, FDR was a big ocean swimmer, Kant was a crazy walker, and I will close with two awesome excerpts from Thoreau, from an essay literally titled:

"Walking"

1. “Moreover, you must walk like a camel, which is said to be the only beast which ruminates when walking. When a traveler asked Wordsworth's servant to show him her master's study, she answered, "Here is his library, but his study is out of doors."

2. I think that I cannot preserve my health and spirits, unless I spend four hours a day at least--and it is commonly more than that--sauntering through the woods and over the hills and fields, absolutely free from all worldly engagements.

---

"Here is his library, but his study is out of doors." -- banger

Spending four hours "sauntering through the woods and over the hills"...that fucking rules, u must be in such a great goddamn mood doing that every day

Saunter Spree

quotedTweet.text:
on getting good sleep; I'm convinced the only thing that matters is putting 4-5 miles on the wheels each day

all the other stuff ppl do, the "sleep hygiene" routines, pale in comparison

0 miles = bad sleep, always
5+ miles = best odds (nothing is guaranteed)

five thoughts:

1. "sleep is more important than diet and exercise combined" - think this is factual/not even up for debate

key is u have to be maniacal about it throughout the day, at least while getting new habits in place

from the moment u wake up "what can I do to make sure I sleep good tonight"

once u get used to getting 8 hrs...and then u get 4, and u see how fucked up u are...u recognize that u are literally impaired. it happens, u just adjust for it - "not a good day for me to operate heavy machinery"

2. on walking 5+ miles...it sounds like a lot but once u aggressively break ur day down and look for any chunk of free time - its doable

it takes 2-3 months to put a new habit in place...they say 66 days or something comically accurate, but I agree, 60-90 days of daily discipline/dedicated focus and u can change ur lifestyle

best way to get there is in 2 blocks
-wake up early, train, move around
-early afternoon + sunshine
-if u can do more then do it...more movement >> better sleep. that 7-9 AM block where the sun is out is the holy grail bc ur body clock adjusts, but life/work tend to get in the way. someday...

3. jamming it into ur day

-take every possible phone call "on the hop"...say "let me call u back in 2 min," put on sneakers, go outside.
-stuff like replying to emails which u can do from ur phone, save for later in the day, then do it while walking around
-every possible "meeting," make it "lets just walk around," instead of lunch/drinks/coffee
-take the stairs everywhere
-if u have to be somewhere at 2 PM, and are free at noon, dont sit around doing nothing til 130 and take an uber...start walking there at noon even if its 20 miles away, knock out 5, then get a car when the timing lines up

4. perception

no one will think u are weird for this kind of shit

or, put another way, the ppl who will think u are weird...are the ppl who its okay to be thought weird by.

obsessive/psycho/high-performing mf's are all on this type of time

read bios of many great thinkers or authors and u see most of them walked insane amounts each day (8-10+ miles)

a lot of ppl who are "in shape," end up that way as an accidental output...they move around a lot to settle their mind and to get good sleep.

training is "for sanity, not vanity." everything is performance-driven, results-driven, output-driven...all these little steps and habits are incremental, they compound.

u have to be freakish and maniacal about this stuff, "put yourself first," dont worry abt perception...esp bc most people's response will be "damn thats actually a good idea."

5. on all the other stuff ppl do

theres nothing wrong w all the sleep masks, noise machines etc, but beyond that, the more natural the better

"there is no consequence-free drug"
"what goes up must come down"

everything u put in ur body that isnt natural will either leave u groggy, or refresh u at 90% and not 100%...all the supplements are nonsense, and all booze/drugs/pills come at a cost, esp caffeine which has a 5-6 hr half-life (ie stop drinking it 10-12 hrs before bed)

END>>

ultimately sleep is frustrating, its a unicorn...sometimes it just doesn’t come. all u can do is put urself in position to succeed.

but thats why I wrote this up...ppl do everything, except the most important thing...MOVE AROUND.

"Our nature consists in motion; complete rest is death." - Pascal
